overall: Atlanta hit a running max of 95.0°F at 15:52 ET, already exceeding the NWS daytime high forecast of 94°F. Temperatures are now falling — the 30-minute velocity is -3.3°F/hr and the current reading at 16:25 ET is 93.2°F — indicating the diurnal peak has passed. Severe thunderstorm activity is developing to the west and northwest (Douglasville/Carroll County area), which may reinforce the cooling trend through outflow boundaries.
forecast_obs_notes: Model guidance was notably spread today: GFS ran hot at 97.8°F while HRRR came in low at 91.1°F, with ECMWF (93.7°F) and NBM (93.1°F) clustered in the middle. The observed running max of 95.0°F beat the ECMWF/NBM consensus by roughly 1.5–2°F but fell well short of the GFS outlier; GFS appears to have been overdone given that temperatures are already declining.
max_temp_prediction: With the peak hour confirmed at 15:52 ET (now ~33 minutes in the past), a -3.3°F/hr cooling rate, and nearby severe thunderstorm activity that could deliver additional outflow cooling, today's TMAX is effectively locked in at 95.0°F. A marginal upside to ~95.5°F is possible only if a brief sun-break re-warms before storms arrive, but this is low probability given current trajectory. For the active odd-bucket Kalshi market, the bucket containing 95°F carries the overwhelming probability mass.
